userStories.title: Preserve dispatch failure on acceptance operation output
acceptanceCriteria: [runSelfHealChain] returns a turn whose adapterFailure.outcome is `fail-service-down` when a seed with that adapterFailure is followed by one corrective turn with no adapterFailure.
[runSelfHealChain] returns a turn whose adapterFailure.outcome is `fail-timeout` when a seed with `fail-service-down` is followed by one corrective turn with its own `fail-timeout` adapterFailure.
[runSelfHealChain] returns a turn with no adapterFailure property when a seed with no adapterFailure is followed by one corrective turn also carrying none.
[runSelfHealChain] returns the seed's output and adapterFailure when a seed carrying adapterFailure has a step that detects nothing and issues no corrective turn.

[callOp] resolves a run-kind operation to a value with `testCode: null` and adapterFailure.outcome `fail-service-down` when its dispatch outcome carries that failure and parse returns `{ testCode: null }`.
[callOp] resolves a run-kind operation to the parsed value with no adapterFailure property when its dispatch outcome carries no adapterFailure.
[callOp] preserves adapterFailure.outcome `fail-quality` when a run-kind dispatch outcome carries `fail-service-down` and parse returns an object already carrying `fail-quality`.
[callOp] resolves to the same string when a run-kind dispatch outcome carries adapterFailure and parse returns a string.

routing.reasoning: Three existing modules need small, conventional metadata-preservation changes; existing operation and self-heal seams support focused unit tests.

userStories.title: Do not fabricate skeletons for dispatch failures
acceptanceCriteria: When acceptanceSetupStage receives `{ testCode: null, adapterFailure: { category: "availability", outcome: "fail-service-down", message: "Upstream idle timeout exceeded", retriable: true } }` from `_acceptanceSetupDeps.callOp` for acceptance-generate, then it makes no `_acceptanceSetupDeps.writeFile` call whose path is the group's acceptance test path.

When acceptanceSetupStage receives that failed generation result, then it emits a warning on the `acceptance-setup` channel whose message differs from `agent did not produce test content; using skeleton` and whose metadata includes outcome `fail-service-down` and `Upstream idle timeout exceeded`.

When acceptanceSetupStage receives `{ testCode: null }` with no adapterFailure, then it writes skeleton content to the group's acceptance test path and emits `agent did not produce test content; using skeleton`, preserving the model-quality path unchanged.
When acceptanceSetupStage receives non-empty testCode together with adapterFailure, then it writes that testCode to the group's acceptance test path.
When acceptanceSetupStage receives the failed generation result while a file already exists at the group's acceptance test path, then that file's content remains unchanged.
When acceptanceStage executes for a package with no acceptance test file and at least one acceptance-enabled story, then it records the package in the acceptance verdict's `missingTargets`.

routing.reasoning: One existing stage’s injected call and file seams support a contained three-way branch and a protected downstream missing-target behavior.

userStories.title: Reject stub-only acceptance regenerations
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make regeneration report failure when setup leaves a stub acceptance test.

**Motivation** — `regenerateAcceptanceTest` decides success by checking only that a file exists at the target path, and the skeleton fallback guarantees one.

**Approach** — `regenerateAcceptanceTest` gains the stub check the acceptance loop already performs one iteration later, so a regeneration that produced only stubs is reported as the failure it is instead of costing a further generation attempt.

**Scope** — In: retain backup and missing-file behavior and reject existing regenerated content classified as a stub. Out: changing retry control. US-003 only: changing `MAX_STUB_REGENS`, the acceptance loop's retry budget, or when the loop decides to regenerate is out of scope. This story changes what a regeneration reports, not how many are attempted. US-003 only: changing the stub-detection predicate itself is out of scope; the existing classifier is used as it stands.

**Interface**
```typescript
function isStubTestFile(content: string): boolean
async function regenerateAcceptanceTest(testPath: string, acceptanceContext: PipelineContext): Promise<boolean>
```

After re-running the acceptance-setup stage, retain the missing-file rejection and add a second rejection: when the file exists but its content is stub content, log at error level with a message distinct from the missing-file one and return `false`. Real regenerated content is unaffected.
acceptanceCriteria: [regenerateAcceptanceTest] returns false when the acceptance-setup stage it invokes leaves stub content at the target path.
[regenerateAcceptanceTest] returns true when the acceptance-setup stage it invokes leaves real test content at the target path.
[regenerateAcceptanceTest] returns false when the acceptance-setup stage it invokes leaves no file at the target path.

When regenerateAcceptanceTest returns false because the target path holds stub content, then it logs at error level on the `acceptance` channel with a message distinct from the error it logs when the file is missing entirely.

When regenerateAcceptanceTest is invoked, then it writes the target path's pre-existing content to a sibling path ending in `.bak` before invoking acceptance-setup, whichever value it goes on to return.

routing.reasoning: A single existing helper adds one post-regeneration predicate and error branch while retaining established backup and missing-file behavior.

userStories.title: Add acceptance and regression gate summary to status files
acceptanceCriteria: [buildStatusSnapshot] returns gates.acceptance `failed` and gates.regression `passed` when state.postRun has acceptance.status `failed` and regression.status `passed`.
[buildStatusSnapshot] returns a snapshot with no `gates` property when state has no postRun.
[buildStatusSnapshot] returns gates.acceptance `failed` when state.postRun has acceptance.status `passed` and non-empty acceptance.skippedPackages.
[buildStatusSnapshot] returns gates.acceptance `passed` when state.postRun has acceptance.status `passed` and acceptance.skippedPackages is absent.
[buildStatusSnapshot] preserves snapshot.run.status equal to the state's runStatus when state.postRun has acceptance.status `failed`.
[buildStatusSnapshot] returns gates.regression `not-run` when state.postRun has regression.status `not-run`.
When writeStatusFile writes a snapshot carrying gates and the file is read back, then parsed gates.acceptance equals the value written.

routing.reasoning: The existing centralized snapshot builder needs an additive derived field and its established unit/integration serialization tests cover the behavior.

analysis:
This is an existing TypeScript feature change. US-001 spans src/operations/self-heal.ts:58, src/operations/call.ts, and src/operations/acceptance-generate.ts. runSelfHealChain currently returns `{ ...last, estimatedCostUsd: totalCost }`, so a corrective TurnResult replaces seed metadata. acceptanceGenerateOp always executes its path-correction self-heal. callOp normalizes the run outcome, records fallbacks, parses output, and returns runPostParse’s result without attaching `outcome.adapterFailure`; the attachment must preserve a parsed object’s own failure and leave non-object parsed values unchanged. call.ts is already 563 lines, so use a small module-private helper at the run tail or move it to existing src/operations/post-parse.ts if needed. AdapterFailure is defined in src/context/engine/types.ts and has four required fields. Existing self-heal coverage is test/unit/operations/self-heal.test.ts; callOp has extensive existing unit fixtures under test/unit/operations/call*.test.ts and run-operation-retry.test.ts.

US-002 changes the generation loop in src/pipeline/stages/acceptance-setup.ts. Its `_acceptanceSetupDeps.callOp` and `writeFile` are established test seams, exercised by test/unit/pipeline/stages/acceptance-setup-agent-file.test.ts. The current result is locally cast as `{ testCode: string | null }` and all falsy results generate a skeleton. The new branch must not write or delete `testPath` on an adapter failure, but must retain the truthy-code path and current no-failure skeleton warning. src/pipeline/stages/acceptance.ts already detects absent required package test paths, adds packageDir to `missingTargets`, stores `ctx.acceptanceFailures`, and returns fail; protect this seam rather than duplicating it.

US-003 is localized to src/execution/lifecycle/acceptance-helpers.ts. regenerateAcceptanceTest already backs up pre-existing content to `.bak`, deletes the original, invokes setup through `_regenerateDeps`, and returns false for a missing target. `isStubTestFile` already exists in this file and must be applied to regenerated existing content. Tests in test/unit/execution/lifecycle/acceptance-loop.test.ts use the injectable regeneration dependencies. Do not alter acceptance-loop retry scheduling or MAX_STUB_REGENS.

US-004 is an additive status schema change in src/execution/status-file.ts. NaxStatusFile already makes postRun optional, and buildStatusSnapshot is the centralized producer for status snapshots. Add optional gates only when `state.postRun` exists; derive acceptance from postRun except that non-empty skippedPackages forces `failed`; preserve `run.status`. Existing serialization and snapshot tests are in test/integration/execution/status-file.test.ts, and status-writer call sites need no migration because derivation is centralized. Old on-disk status files remain readable because gates is optional and is not backfilled.
outOfScope: Retrying or swapping the agent when acceptance generation fails to dispatch is out of scope. Manager-tier retry was settled in #1869 and #1870 and further work is tracked in #1884; this feature changes what a failed dispatch is reported as, not how many times it is attempted.

US-002 only: deleting or rolling back an acceptance test file that already exists at the target path when a regeneration dispatch fails is out of scope. The branch writes nothing; it does not remove prior content.
US-002 only: propagating the dispatch failure as a thrown error that aborts the run is out of scope. The stage records the failure and lets the existing missing-target path fail the acceptance gate.

US-001 only: attaching the run outcome's `adapterFailure` to the outputs of operations other than `acceptance-generate` is a consequence of `callOp` being shared, but no other operation's behaviour is changed to read it here.
US-001 only: carrying an `adapterFailure` through the `complete`-kind branch of `callOp` is out of scope; the acceptance generator is a `run`-kind operation.

US-003 only: changing `MAX_STUB_REGENS`, the acceptance loop's retry budget, or when the loop decides to regenerate is out of scope. This story changes what a regeneration reports, not how many are attempted.
US-003 only: changing the stub-detection predicate itself is out of scope; the existing classifier is used as it stands.

US-004 only: changing the meaning of `run.status`, adding a new value such as `completed-with-failures`, or changing the values of `PostRunPhaseStatus` is out of scope. This story adds an additive summary field and leaves every existing value alone.
US-004 only: surfacing `gates` in the TUI, the headless run footer, or the `nax status` command is out of scope; this story writes the field into the status file.
US-004 only: including the `finish` phase in `gates` is out of scope — `postRun.finish` is optional and describes what happened after the gates, not a gate.
Backfilling `gates` onto status files already written to disk is out of scope.
Changing the auto-commit that the acceptance-setup stage performs is out of scope; with US-002 landed there is simply no stub file for it to commit on the dispatch-failure path.
